findings.summary: isPublished(article) returns false whenever article is undefined (target slug not found in the articles map), and the caller treats that identically to a real unpublished post — stripping the link and logging it as 'stripped ... link(s) to unpublished post(s)'. This conflates 'target doesn't exist' with 'target isn't published yet'. Verified by running the plugin directly against a link to /blog/2 (a plausible pagination-style path under the site's own /blog/[...page] route, since the regex `^/blog/([^/?#]+)` matches any single path segment, not just post slugs): the plugin silently downgrades it to plain text and logs '[draft-links] some-post3.mdx: stripped 1 link(s) to unpublished post(s): 2', even though '2' isn't a post at all. In practice this means any typo'd or non-post /blog/<x> link in a post body is silently swallowed into inert plain text with a misleading log message, rather than surfacing as a broken link for the author to notice and fix.

findings.summary: The comment says this 'Mirrors apps/web/src/utils/data-utils.ts', but the real isPublished() there is `!data.draft && (import.meta.env.DEV || data.publishDate.getTime() <= Date.now() + BRISBANE_OFFSET_MS)` — every other consumer of the rule (index, tag pages, blog listing, RSS) treats a future-dated non-draft post as published while running `pnpm dev`. This plugin's reimplementation drops the DEV branch entirely, so during local dev a link to a future-dated post would still get stripped/logged as unpublished even though every other page on the dev site is already showing that post as live. No impact on production build output (DEV is always false there), so this only affects the local-preview experience, not what ships.

findings.summary: The implementer's report states 'Tests for the change were written and run,' but the diff adds no test file, and the repo has no test framework at all (no vitest/jest config, no *.test.* or *.spec.* file anywhere in the tree). Whatever verification was actually done, it wasn't a written/runnable test as claimed.
